texts.preamble: M/S Cargil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2016 -1- M. Cr. C. No.3517/2012 07/01/2016
texts.facts: The petitioner before this Court has filed this present petition under Sec.482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for quashment of complaint bearing Criminal Case No.6565/2008 filed by the State of Madhya Pradesh against the petitioner. 2- The petition is also against the order dated 26/08/2008 (Annex.-P/1) by which the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ujjain has taken cognizance of the offence punishable under Sec.7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. 3- The facts of the case reveal that the petitioners are engaged in the manufacturing business of Vegetable Oil and on 18/12/2006, the sample was taken from the retailer. The sample was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst on 19/12/2006 and a report dated 15/01/2007 of Public Analyst was received. Notice under Sec.13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was given to the Company on 28/08/2008 and the 'Best Before' date of the sample is 12 months from packing. The aforesaid fact is an undisputed fact. The report of the Public Analyst which is on record itself makes it very clear that the 'Best Before' date is 12 months from packing, meaning thereby, the shelf life of 12 months was over in the month of October, 2007 itself. A notice was given to the petitioner on 28/08/2008 under Sec.13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and by that time the shelf life was already over. The same reads as under:- "The petitioners before this Court has filed this present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the complaint bearing criminal case No. 1500/2005 filed by the State of M.P. against the petitioners/Company. The petition is also against the order dated 09.11.2005 passed by Chief judicial Magistrate at Vidisha taking cognizance of the offences punishable under Section 7(i)/7(v) read with Section 16(i)(a)(i) (ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The facts of the case reveal that the petitioners were engaged in manufacturing for sale, distributing, storing and selling of food articles including Sweetened Carbonated M/S Cargil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28341246/ 1 Beverages under various brands and Packaged Drinking Water under the brand namely "Kinley". On 31.05.2005, the Food Inspector inspected the shop of Kamini Enterprises situated at Baripura Kiri Mohalla Vidisha and took the sample of "Kinley Packaged Drinking Water 1 litre", manufactured by Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverage Pvt. Ltd./petitioner No. 1, Batch No. 015, packed on 16.04.2005, best before six months from manufacture for the purpose of analysis. Thereafter the Food Inspector prepared form No. VI a per Rule 12 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. A panchnama was also prepared by the Food Inspector. Thereafter the sample was sent to the Public Analyst on 31.05.2005. The Food Inspector received the report of Public Analyst on 02.07.2005 vide letter dated 10.08.2005. The Food Inspector received the permission to file complaint on 28.10.2005. The complaint was filed on 09.11.2005.
texts.arguments: 4- The ground raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner before this Court is that the shelf life of Vegetable Oil is one year and the same expired on October, 2007 and therefore, he has been deprived of his right under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for getting sample and therefore, the entire complaint deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 5- Learned counsel for the petitioner has also placed reliance upon the judgment delivered by this Court in the case of Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. Vs. State of M. P. passed in M.Cr.C.No.12155/2014 . The ground raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners before this Court is that as the shelf life of Kinley Drinking Water was six months and it expired on 16.10.2005. He has been deprived of his right under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for getting the sample re-examined and therefor, entire complaint deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. He has placed reliance upon the judgment delivered by this Court in case of Inderjit Walia Vs. State of M.P. passed in M.Cr.C.No.8517/2014. His contention is in the similar circumstances by taking into account the various judgment delivered by the Apex Court the learned Single Judge has [LEAKAGE_MASK] the complaint. This Court in the case of Inderjit Walia (supra) in paragraphs 4 to 11 has held as under: "4. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submits that it is evident from Panchanama prepared by the Food Inspector that packet of 'Ajwain Cookies' was packed on "27.08.2010" and it may be used before six months from the date of packing i.e. "26.02.2011" and the other sample of 'Mix Choco Cookies' manufacturing date is "16.11.2010" and expiry date is "16.01.2011"; whereas this complaint has been filed on 23.09.2011. Thus, the complaint has been filed after the expiry period of use of these samples. In such circumstances the petitioner has been deprived of his valuable right under Section 13(2) of the Act to send the other part of the sample to the Director, Central Food Laboratory for analysis. In such circumstances the order of taking cognizance of the offences against the petitioner is not sustainable in law. Learned Senior Counsel for this purpose cited the judgments of this Court in Misc. Criminal Case No. 2049 of 2012 [Glaxo Smith Kline Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v/s State of Madhya Pradesh ] decided on 05.12.2012 and Misc. Criminal Case No. 5580 of 2012 [I.T.C. Ltd. and another v/s State of M.P.] decided on 05.12.2012. He also cited the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Gupta Chemicals Private Limited and others v/s State of Rajasthan and another [(2010) 7 SCC 735] and submitted that the M/S Cargil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28341246/ 2 shelf life of the product had expired when the complaint was filed. Therefore, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is not sustainable in law. In such circumstances, the order of taking cognizance for the offences under Sections 7(1) and 16(1)(a)(i) of the Act be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and discharged the petitioner from the charges. 5. Although several grounds have been raised in the petition, but learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner has confined his arguments in regard to Section 13(2) of the Act. 8. This Court in the case of ITC Limited and another (Supra) has dealt with this issue and held as under:- "in the present case, the panchnama prepared by the Food Inspector shows that on the packets of "Mittal's Premium Cherry Karonda Murrabba" it has been mentioned that it is best before 6 months from the date of packing and it was best before six months from the date of manufacuring, therefore, it is clear that after one and half years from the date of sampling complaint has been filed on 13.04.2011 and petitioner has been deprived of his right of second sampling as the products were expired much before the date of complaint, therefore, considering the judgments cited above, the proceedings pending against the petitioners before the trial Court are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]." 9. Adverting to the facts of the case, it may be observed that the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act along with the copy of the report of the Public Analyst was forwarded to the petitioner No. 1 on 29.07.2011 i.e. nearly a year after the expiry of the shelf life of the sample. Bhajan Lal AIR 1992 SC 604, attracting interference under the inherent powers."
